issues.failure_explanation: The hypothesis $\|\Pp_{\Ff_N}\phi-\phi\|_{\Ff}=\mathcal{O}(N^{-\alpha})$ for ALL $\phi\in\Ff$ cannot hold when $\Ff$ is infinite-dimensional: the $\Ff_N$ are proper finite-dimensional subspaces, so $\|\mathrm{Id}-\Pp_{\Ff_N}\|=1$ for every $N$, and a diagonal argument (unit vectors $v_k\perp\Ff_{N_k}$ with $N_k$ growing fast) produces $\phi\in\Ff$ whose projection error decays slower than any prescribed rate. Hence Corollary order corollary and part 2 of Theorems OC theorem and OC theorem noise are vacuous outside the trivial finite-dimensional case (where the error is eventually zero). Moreover, the claimed constant control cannot hold under any nontrivial uniform reading (it would force $\|\mathrm{Id}-\Pp_{\Ff_N}\|\le CN^{-\alpha}$), and the proof of OC theorem derives only '$\lesssim\|\Aa\|\|f\|_{\Dd}\varepsilon$' with an unspecified constant rather than the stated '$\le\|\Aa\|\|f\|_{\Dd}\varepsilon$'; since always $\|\Aa\|\le1$, the sampling term $\varepsilon\|f\|_{\Dd}$ alone already exceeds the stated bound whenever $\|\Aa\|<1$.

failure_location.quote: Consider $\Psi_N$ satisfying Assumption \ref{assumption} and such that $ \norm{\Pp_{\Ff_N} \phi-\phi}_\Ff = \mathcal{O}(N^{-\alpha}) $ for all $\phi\in \Ff$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate the rate hypotheses pointwise for the functions involved (a rate for $f$ in $\Dd$-norm and for $\Aa f$ in $\Ff$-norm), allow the hidden constants to depend on those functions' approximation profiles, and weaken the part-2 bounds to $\lesssim$-form absorbing the $\varepsilon\|f\|_{\Dd}$ term; the convergence rates then survive for functions possessing the assumed rates.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised explicit convergence rates and the quantitative bounds $\|\wh{\Aa}_{NM}\Pp_{\Dd_N}f-\Aa f\|_{\Ff}\le\|\Aa\|\|f\|_{\Dd}\varepsilon$ (noiseless and noisy versions) are not established for any nontrivial infinite-dimensional system. Part 1 of Theorems OC theorem and OC theorem noise (the bound on $\|\wh{\Aa}_{NM}-\Aa_N\|$) is unaffected.
issues.title: Rate results rest on an unsatisfiable 'for all phi' hypothesis and uncontrolled constants
issues.why_classification: The repair is local and preserves the rates and proof structure, but the stated scope ('for all $\phi\in\Ff$') and the explicit constant $\|\Aa\|\|f\|_{\Dd}$ in the error bound are necessarily withdrawn, so the stated guarantees are only partially preserved.

issues.failure_explanation: For a FEM mass matrix with respect to a probability measure, $\|\bm{G}_N\|=\Theta(h^d)=\Theta(1/N)$ and $\|\bm{G}_N^{-1}\|=\Theta(N)$ in any dimension (e.g. in one dimension $\bm{G}_N=h[\frac23\,\mathrm{diag}+\frac16\,\mathrm{off}]$ has spectrum in $[h/3,h]$, so $\|\bm{G}_N^{-1}\|=\Theta(h^{-1})=\Theta(N)$). The equality $\Oo(h_N^{-1})=\Oo(N^{1/2})$ is wrong: in one dimension $h^{-1}\sim N$, and in two dimensions $h^{-1}=N^{1/2}$ but then $\|\bm{G}_N^{-1}\|=\Theta(h^{-2})$. With the correct scaling $\|\bm{G}_N^{-1}\|=O(N)$, the derived rates become $M=O(\varepsilon^{-2-4/\alpha})$ and cost $O(\varepsilon^{-2-5/\alpha})$, so the concluding claim of cost parity with the dense example ($\varepsilon^{-2-3/\alpha}$) is false.

issues.failure_explanation: Since $\bm{g}=\Psi_N(\bm{x})+\bm{\eta}$ (and $\bm{c}=\Aa\Psi_N(\bm{x})+$ noise), independence and zero mean give $\mathbb{E}[\bm{g}\bm{g}^\dagger]=\bm{G}_N+\mathbb{E}[\bm{\eta}\bm{\eta}^\dagger]$ and $\mathbb{E}[\bm{c}\bm{g}^\dagger]=\bm{C}_N+\mathbb{E}[\bm{\xi}\bm{\eta}^\dagger]$, which equal $\bm{G}_N$ and $\bm{C}_N$ only for zero noise; the identities (gcmatdef) are false premises, the summands in (sum def) are not centred, and Bernstein's inequality does not apply. Decisively, $\tl{\bm{G}}_{NM}\to\bm{G}_N+\mathbb{E}[\eta\eta^\dagger]$ and $\tl{\bm{C}}_{NM}\to\bm{C}_N+\mathbb{E}[\xi\eta^\dagger]$ almost surely, so $\tl{\Aa}_{NM}$ converges to $(\bm{C}_N+\mathbb{E}[\xi\eta^\dagger])(\bm{G}_N+\mathbb{E}[\eta\eta^\dagger])^{-1}\neq\Aa_N$ in general (e.g. independent Gaussian noise of variance $\sigma^2$ gives the limit $\bm{C}_N(\bm{G}_N+\sigma^2\bm{I})^{-1}$). The claimed high-probability bound with arbitrarily small $\delta$ therefore fails for all sufficiently large $M$. (Also, (gcdef) adds the dictionary noise $\bm{\eta}_N^m$ instead of the operator noise $\bm{\xi}_N^m$ to $\Aa\Psi_N(\bm{x}_m)$.)
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must account for the non-vanishing noise-covariance bias, e.g. by debiasing the estimators (subtracting a known noise covariance), by letting the noise variance vanish with $M$, or by restating the bounds with an irreducible bias term, and then rederiving the concentration argument.
issues.overall_effect: Proposition noise bound, Theorem OC theorem noise (both parts), the complexity display (order of convergence noise), and the claim that the noisy approximations converge to the true dynamics are unreliable; the paper's noise extension (Contribution 4, abstract) is not established.
issues.title: Noisy estimators are biased: the convergence claim of Proposition noise bound is false
issues.why_classification: With fixed-variance noise the noisy approximations provably do not converge to $\Aa_N$; every supported repair changes the estimator, the noise model, or the guarantee type (convergence to $\Aa_N$ is lost), so the advertised noise-robustness contribution cannot be preserved.

issues.failure_explanation: The conditioning event $\{|(\bm{\eta}_N^m,\bm{\xi}_N^m)|^2\le\tl{\gamma}_N\ \forall m\}$ has probability $\tl{p}_N^{\,M}$ (i.i.d. noise across $m$), not $\tl{p}_N$. The correct relation is $\mathbb{P}[A]\ge\tl{p}_N^{M}\,\tl{\mathbb{P}}[A]$, and since $\tl{p}_N^{M}<\tl{p}_N$ for $M\ge2$, the asserted inequality $\tl{p}_N\tl{\mathbb{P}}\le\mathbb{P}$ is false (take $A$ equal to the conditioning event itself). Hence the chain $p\le\tl{p}_N\tl{\mathbb{P}}[E]\le\mathbb{P}[E]$ fails; the correct bound is only $\mathbb{P}[E]\ge p\,\tl{p}_N^{M-1}<p$. Since $\tl{p}_N^{M}\to0$ as $M\to\infty$, the conditioning strategy is structurally unable to deliver probability bounds that improve with $M$.

issues.failure_explanation: $|(\bm{\eta}_N,\bm{\xi}_N)|^2=\sigma^2\chi^2_{2N}$ (2N independent Gaussians), so with $\tl{\gamma}_N=\sigma^2\gamma_N$ and $\gamma_N=2N$ the correct value is $\tl{p}_N=\mathbb{P}[\chi^2_{2N}\le2N]\to\tfrac12$, not the $\chi^2_N$ tail $1-F_N(\gamma_N)$ used in the displayed chain (the invoked tail bound applies to $\chi^2_N$ beyond twice its mean, not to the $\chi^2_{2N}$ lower-tail at its mean, which is about $1/2$). The chain is also internally inconsistent (first $\tl{p}_N\le(2/e)^{N/2}$, then $\tl{p}_N\ge1-(2/e)^{N/2}$), and the concluding claim $\tl{p}_N\approx1$ is false for the stated truncation level (it fails already for $N\approx6$).

issues.why_classification: A local recomputation with a standard adjustment of the truncation constant preserves the example's qualitative message (noise enters through a constant factor); no other result depends on it beyond the already-defective noise bounds.

issues.failure_explanation: Boundedness of each individual operator $\wh{\Aa}_{NM}$ does not imply boundedness of the eigenvalue sequence $(\lambda_M)$, and part 1 of the theorem assumes only a.e.\ continuity of $\psi_n,\Aa\psi_n$ (no i.i.d.\ sampling, no linear independence). Without sampling assumptions the eigenvalues can diverge: e.g.\ $N=1$, $\psi_1\equiv1$, $\Aa 1=w$ continuous, unbounded and in $L^2(\mu)$, with samples at points where $w$ grows, gives $\lambda_M=\wh{\bm{A}}_{11}\to\infty$, so no convergent subsequence exists and part 1 is false as stated. (Under the full Assumption \ref{assumption} the matrices converge a.s.\ and boundedness holds; part 2 already assumes this.)

failure_location.quote: Additionally, for each $M$, $\wh{\Aa}_{NM}$ is bounded and thus the sequence of eigenvalues $(\lambda_{M})$ is also bounded and has a convergent subsequence.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add Assumption \ref{assumption} (in particular i.i.d.\ sampling and linear independence) to the hypotheses of part 1; the a.s.\ convergence $\wh{\bm{A}}_{NM}\to\bm{A}_N^{\Psi}$ then yields a.s.\ boundedness of the eigenvalues.
issues.overall_effect: Part 1 of the theorem (existence of a convergent subsequence of eigenpairs) is unreliable under its stated hypotheses; the eigenpair-identification of part 2 inherits the gap whenever its additional assumptions are not in force.
issues.title: Data-limit eigensystem theorem: eigenvalue subsequence existence is not established under the stated hypotheses

This is because the subspace spanned by the monomial basis functions is invariant under the Koopman generator of the OU system, see Corollary~\ref{exact approximation}.

issues.failure_explanation: Boundedness of each finite-dimensional $\Aa_N$ does not give a uniform bound, so the eigenvalue sequence need not have a convergent subsequence. Counterexample within the paper's own setting: for the OU generator with the invariant monomial dictionary (which satisfies Assumptions \ref{assumption}, \ref{moments assumption} and \ref{projection assumption}), $\Aa_N=\restr{\Ll}{\Ff_N}$ is triangular with eigenvalues $0,-1,\dots,-(N-1)$; taking $\lambda_N=-(N-1)$ with $\Dd$-normalized eigenfunctions gives $\lambda_N\to-\infty$, contradicting the asserted convergent subsequence ($\|\Aa_N\|_{\Dd\to\Dd}$ involves $\Aa\Aa$ and is unbounded in $N$). Additionally, the weak-compactness step (Banach--Alaoglu in $\Dd$) requires $\Aa$ closed so that $\Dd$ is a Hilbert space (not assumed), and the proof's step (c1d) manipulates an adjoint $\Aa^*g$ that is not defined for general $g\in\Dd$.

failure_location.quote: Additionally, for each $N$, $\Aa_N$ is bounded. Thus, the sequence of eigenvalues $(\lambda_{N})$ is also bounded and has a convergent subsequence.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypotheses that the eigenvalue sequence is bounded, that $\Aa$ is closed (so $\Dd$ is Hilbert), and that $\Dd$ is dense in $\Ff$; the remaining steps are then repairable by routine arguments (Riesz representation for (c1d), self-adjointness of the projection for (c2d)).
issues.overall_effect: The theorem's conclusion (subsequential convergence of eigenpairs of $\Aa_N$ to an eigenpair of $\Aa$) is not valid as stated; unbounded spectral branches, which are generic for generators with unbounded spectrum, are not covered.
issues.title: Dictionary-limit eigensystem theorem is false: eigenvalues of the Galerkin approximations need not be bounded
issues.why_classification: The repaired theorem (subsequential weak convergence for bounded eigenpair sequences) is a recognizable, standard-form spectral approximation result obtained by adding standard hypotheses, but the unconditional subsequence-existence claim must be withdrawn.

issues.failure_explanation: $(f_{NM})$ is bounded ($\|f_{NM}\|_{\Dd}=1$), but $(\lambda_{NM})$ need not be: although $\wh{\Aa}_{NM}\to\Aa_N$ as $M\to\infty$ for fixed $N$, $\sup_N\|\Aa_N\|_{\Dd\to\Dd}$ is typically infinite, and in the paper's own OU/monomial setting eigenpairs with eigenvalues near $-(N-1)$ exist for all large $M$, so a family with $\lambda_{NM}\to-\infty$ has no convergent eigenvalue subsequence. Moreover part 1 assumes only a.e.\ continuity, so $\Dd$ need not be complete (closedness of $\Aa$ is not assumed) and weak compactness of $(f_{NM})$ in $\Dd$ is unjustified.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: let $({\lambda}_{N M}, f_{N M})_{(N,M)\in\N^2} $ be a sequence of eigenvalue and normalized eigenfunction pairs of $\wh{\Aa}_{NM}$.

issues.failure_explanation: The theorem quantifies over an arbitrary doubly-indexed family selecting one eigenpair of $\wh{\Aa}_{NM}$ per index pair, and then claims convergence of the family's values $(\lambda_{N_iM'_{N_i}},f_{N_iM'_{N_i}})$ for every data-size sequence $M'_{N_i}\ge M_{N_i}$. Nothing forces consistency of the selection across $M$: for the OU generator with the invariant monomial dictionary, $\wh{\Aa}_{NM}$ has eigenvalues near $-1$ and near $-2$ for all large $M$, and a family choosing the eigenpair nearest $-1$ for even $M$ and nearest $-2$ for odd $M$ makes $\lambda_{N_iM'_{N_i}}$ oscillate along suitable $M'_{N_i}$, so no subsequence with the stated property exists. The proof never addresses this: it only (invalidly) asserts boundedness and then analyses an already-convergent sequence, so it establishes at most subsequential convergence of a selected family, not the stated 'for any $M'_{N_i}\ge M_{N_i}$' robustness (legitimate at the operator level in Theorem \ref{joint limit theorem} only because that convergence is in operator norm; eigenpair selections admit no such uniformity, especially near multiple eigenvalues).
